## Requirement coverage

| Req | Description | Task(s) | Gap justification |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| R1 | `umpire-backend-process` owns the moved support and a Rust supervisor; TLA+ contains no process implementation or Python; TLA+, TLC and Apalache use the new owner without an Apalache-to-TLC dependency. Native caller contracts preserve functional typed failure/status mapping, Java pin, capture/dump/scratch contracts and platform behavior; old signatures, reexports and diagnostic bytes are not required solely for backward compatibility. Errors: unsupported platforms and unsafe Darwin identity refuse at admission; launch, signal, timeout, cancellation and owner EOF controls retain their outcomes; actual Linux direct/escaped descendants are gone before return; output substitution, malformed UTF-8, bounded reads and cleanup failures retain their checks. The unsafe policy compiles without weakening other crates. | fn-247-one-language-for-the-framework-a-rust.1, fn-247-one-language-for-the-framework-a-rust.4 | — |
| R2 | xtask replaces active helper and embedded Python responsibilities with documented native Rust arguments, schemas, grammar, limits and errors; shell/Make callers are updated coherently. Compiler-input identities are deterministic, portable and stable, with new formats/cache invalidation permitted. Necessary guest/golden/pin regeneration records its cause and old/new hashes; rebuilt current-input artifacts are reproducible and freshness passes. Errors: malformed inputs/TOML/JSON/sidecars, missing/ambiguous closures, native-macro collisions, missing/probe-failed tools, stale artifacts, launch/compiler failures, installation hashes/locks/symlinks/concurrency and malformed retired-name streams retain meaningful negative controls. Minimal cold bootstrap disables auto-install before its first probe and fails clearly; Rust owns semantic validation, with no duplicated Bash parser or old CI freshness skip matrix. Python quirks, exact old diagnostics and byte-parity proofs are retired explicitly. | fn-247-one-language-for-the-framework-a-rust.2, fn-247-one-language-for-the-framework-a-rust.5, fn-247-one-language-for-the-framework-a-rust.6, fn-247-one-language-for-the-framework-a-rust.7 | — |
| R3 | Every useful existing Python test responsibility and Rust control that constructs Python children has a Rust-owned counterpart; the ordinary gate executes those controls and invokes no Python; no tracked Python file remains under the active Model tree. Record pure Python-quirk assertions retired under the owner amendment rather than recreating them. The byte-only retained-original hash verifier and active hash manifest are removed; semantic lifecycle comparison and its mutation control remain. Errors: a changed original lifecycle edge fails; platform-limited controls are reported honestly; no deletion of a safety control or frozen original satisfies this criterion. | fn-247-one-language-for-the-framework-a-rust.2, fn-247-one-language-for-the-framework-a-rust.3, fn-247-one-language-for-the-framework-a-rust.4, fn-247-one-language-for-the-framework-a-rust.5, fn-247-one-language-for-the-framework-a-rust.6, fn-247-one-language-for-the-framework-a-rust.7 | — |

Errors: unmet dependency admission remains explicit; missing platform evidence and timing overruns are reported honestly; no historical byte-parity or redundant full-gate receipt is required. | fn-247-one-language-for-the-framework-a-rust.1, fn-247-one-language-for-the-framework-a-rust.3, fn-247-one-language-for-the-framework-a-rust.8 | — |
| R5 | The canonical `model-validate` entrypoint executes exactly one complete TLC-required Model gate, including all current stages, followed by the existing edited-checker benchmark once. Required Apalache mode remains independently selectable and runs its existing controls inside that same gate. Existing `model-check` and `model-time` commands retain their arguments, mode behavior and failure contracts; focused controls preserve absent/default and explicit-skip semantics. Actual mode, commands, stages and timings are recorded honestly, with required timing identified separately from historical default timing. Errors: conflicting environment/command-line/MAKEFLAGS values cannot turn canonical TLC validation into a skip; gate failure prevents the benchmark; gate and benchmark failures retain both child diagnostic texts and propagate their established statuses at direct-wrapper and GNU Make boundaries; timing overruns remain soft warnings and never hide a failed check; no cached/fabricated pass or omitted stage discharges validation. | fn-247-one-language-for-the-framework-a-rust.3, fn-247-one-language-for-the-framework-a-rust.8 | — |

The audited unsafe site count decreases, recorded before/after.
